referee_caveats_inferred: Ejecta mass depends strongly on the assumed composition (factor ~5 between crystalline and amorphous), and the favored crystalline choice rests on indirect argument
Asteroid flux subtraction relies on one 5-minute pre-impact point and an emissivity assumed equal for both bodies and constant to the impact date
Aperture photometry is applied to an extended source with unmodelled visibility structure; MRS filtering makes masses lower limits
Differing flux calibrators across executions, including one corrected by hand, may leave a systematic flux scale offset beyond the adopted 10%
Gas limits assume Trot = 1000 K and a 2 km/s line width, so limits are model-dependent

missing_for_reproduction: Imaging cell size, image size, niter and thresholds
Continuum spectral-window selection and line-free channel handling
Exact aperture centers and flux summation procedure
Epsilon (infrared emissivity) value and size split used in NEATM
No public statement of data availability or product location in the paper text
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly 20-100 GB for nine short Band 7 executions (1 pre-impact 12 m, 4 post-impact 12 m, 4 ACA); estimate
reproducibility.score_reason: Project code, CASA version, calibrators, weighting and nearly all model parameters, equations and numeric results are given; imaging grid, masks, auto_selfcal settings and flux-summation details are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Single ALMA project with stated executions, explicit thermal and dust-mass recipe and numeric results (emissivity, masses, upper limits); archive data presumably public but paper does not state it.
